title: Stream resilience: fast-fail reconnect probe and persistent commit-log for client-led resumes
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a fast-fail reconnect probe to reduce client-observed stall windows; adds a small persistent commit-log for stream resume checkpoints; no API breaking changes; rollout: gradual 5%->50%->100% across regions; note: requires client SDK patch for best results.
description: Motivation: production users reported long tail stalls when clients lost connectivity and reconnected immediately; the service would keep inflight resources for the previous session until server lease expired which increased latency and token waste. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a lightweight fast-fail reconnect probe that lets clients detect a stale server session lease and trigger a low-cost soft-abort locally, and 2) a small persistent commit-log per-stream (bounded to 64 entries) that records checkpoint metadata (prefix hash, last acked index, tool-call idempotency tokens) to allow deterministic client-led resume without server-side full session replay. Design constraints: keep OpenAI-compat streaming semantics intact, maintain idempotency for function/tool calls, and ensure no unbounded server memory growth. Implementation: added stream/commitlog service (inference/runtime/commitlog.go) implementing an append-only, ring-backed append with TTL eviction and metadata compaction; added probe handshake extension to the websocket/streaming protocol (api/compat/stream_probe.go) with two-phase probe: SYN (client) -> SYN-ACK (server lease + lease-version) -> FAST-ACK (client decision to continue or soft-abort). On soft-abort clients are instructed to issue a resume token against the commit-log rather than relying solely on server KV-cache. API compatibility: handshake extension is optional and backward compatible; servers that do not understand probe will continue to behave as today. Migration and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag stream.fast_fail_probe (default off). QA & rollout plan: unit + e2e tests included, staged deploy to canary cluster for 48h, followed by region ramp. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-2048) [x] unit tests [x] e2e stream recovery tests [x] SDK updates queued (Python/TS) [x] docs update (api/streaming.md) Related: addresses customer SUP-4821 and reduces incident recurrence for INC-2026. For reviewers: focus on (a) lease/version handling race conditions, (b) commit-log eviction semantics, (c) tool-call idempotency guarantees during resume.

extend streaming handshake with fast-fail probe frames
runtime: integrate probe flow into session lifecycle and lease checks
compat: add probe parsing and fallback behavior for legacy clients
tests: unit + e2e for probe and resume flows
docs: update streaming API docs and migration notes
review_threads: Arjun Patel: Left a couple of nits around the commit-log compaction window; main concern is what happens when a client holds on to a resume token past the ring wrap; suggestion: attach token generation epoch and validate against lease-version. Author (Maya): responded that tokens include epoch and the server validates token. Added tests for epoch mismatch.

Lena Ortiz: Asked for clarity on metrics - added counters for probe-sent, probe-accepted, probe-rejected, soft-aborts, resume-success/failure; please confirm labels and dashboards. Author: added metrics and dashboard PR pointer.

Tomás Rivera: Observed a potential race where server lease refresh could happen concurrently with probe SYN processing causing a false-reject and client unnecessary soft-abort. Requested a small retry window on the server side (100ms) and documented in code comments. Author: implemented and added integration test that simulates lease refresh race.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash-merge by Maya Chen. Commit message: 'stream: fast-fail probe + commit-log for client resumes; add tests and docs'
migration_instructions: Enable runtime flag stream.fast_fail_probe=false in canary, then enable true on 5% of nodes. Ensure SDKs are updated in client releases to include probe support; clients without SDK update will continue using legacy behavior. Operators: monitor metrics stream.probe.* and stream.resume.fail_rate and rollback if resume.fail_rate > 0.1%.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover commitlog append/evict and token epoch semantics. E2E includes simulated client disconnects at random offsets with network partitioning; validated tool-call exactly-once constraints via idempotency tokens. Load tests show <1% additional p99 latency for handshake on warm sessions and 20-40ms improvement in median recovery time in tested scenarios.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: probe is opt-in and commit-log size is bounded. Follow-up tasks: SDK patches merge (PRs queued in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript), add optional encrypted commit-log for Private deployments, and add diagnostic traces for lease-version mismatches.
